verdict.rationale: Isaac Sim is itself a simulated test environment. The docs say developers can 'evaluate the end-to-end system in Isaac Sim using software-in-the-loop or hardware-in-the-loop testing,' 'validate robot stacks with ROS 2,' and plug into existing testing pipelines, so robot stacks can be exercised away from real deployments. The evidence never frames this as isolation from production data or systems, and there is nothing on separating sandbox from production environments, data, or credentials. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of isolation from production data/systems, sandbox-versus-production environment separation controls, independent hands-on corroboration of sandboxed agent testing.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: developers can train perception and mobility stacks in simulation and evaluate the end-to-end system in Isaac Sim using software-in-the-loop or hardware-in-the-loop testing.
integrate framework capabilities into existing testing and validation pipelines.
